walkthroughs.body_html:
Radiation is heat as infrared waves (a kind of light).

It travels through a vacuum - that's how the Sun heats us across empty space.

All warm objects emit infrared. Your body glows in infrared all the time!

Dark, matt surfaces are good absorbers and emitters of radiation. Wear black on a cold day, you'll absorb the Sun.

Shiny, light surfaces are good reflectors. Wear white in summer, you'll stay cool.

Houses paint roofs and tanks white in hot countries to reflect away the heat.

A vacuum flask keeps drinks hot all day by blocking all three heat transfers:

Conduction - the vacuum between the walls has no particles.
Convection - no fluid to flow.
Radiation - shiny silver walls reflect infrared back in.

Genius design from over 100 years ago!

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between a real image and a virtual image?
options: Velocity is always conserved in any collision.
A real image is formed where light rays actually converge and can be projected on a screen; a virtual image is where rays only appear to come from and cannot be projected.
A real image is in colour and a virtual image is black and white.
A real image is solid and a virtual image is transparent.

mcqs.q: In a collision between two objects, what quantity is always conserved (in a closed system)?
options: Velocity is always conserved in any collision.
Yes — half-life is the time between each emission from the source.
Kinetic energy is always conserved in collisions because energy is conserved.
Total momentum is always conserved; kinetic energy is only conserved in elastic collisions.
